b3 = [-0.133, -0.132, 0.084, -0.172, -0.073]

which promotes no-op/up. This indicates the network learned meaningful preferences among all four directions, not just left/right. The presence of channel 1 (“moving objects”) and channel 4 (“previous frame”) together suggests the game contains autonomous moving entities whose velocity matters.

Reasoning: The five channels match a game with an agent, autonomous moving objects, collectible reward targets, walls/obstacles, and a previous-frame channel. This rules out simple maze or Snake-like games where there are no other moving objects, and Pong-like games where there are no reward targets in the grid. Breakout is less likely because the agent only moves left/right, yet the output biases make up/down distinct and meaningful. Sokoban is also less likely because boxes are passive and goals are not directly rewarding to the agent. The best fit is a Pac-Man-style game: the agent controls Pac-Man, ghosts are the moving objects, pellets are the reward targets, maze walls are obstacles, and the previous frame tracks Pac-Man and ghosts.
